WHO.title: Who decides for Quispicanchi?
WHO.question: Seven decisions that shape life in the South Valley. Who made each one: the comunidad, Cusco, or Lima?

decisions.detail: Most land is held through the comunidad campesina, not as private titles, and families farm small plots scattered across the mountain.

decisions.q: When the irrigation canals are cleaned
decisions.detail: Canals are kept up by faenas, communal work days the community organizes.

decisions.q: How the Cusco tourist-ticket money is split
decisions.detail: National law splits it: 40% to district towns, 30% to the Ministry of Culture, 20% to provinces and 10% to regional tourism.

decisions.q: Whether towns may spend ticket money on clean water
decisions.detail: The national rules limit what the money may pay for. The Comptroller found ten Cusco towns, Quispicanchi among them, spent S/104 million on uses not allowed, such as water and sanitation (2018–19).
A national program, Wasi Mikuna, served 204,560 students in 4,105 Cusco schools at the end of 2024.
A national vote: Keiko Fujimori won the runoff with 50.1%, carried by metropolitan Lima, while the south voted heavily for Roberto Sánchez.

decisions.q: Bringing agencies together on femicide and family violence in the region
decisions.detail: In September 2026 Cusco's regional governor convened the region's agencies to act on femicide and family violence.

WHO.notice: The comunidad decides a great deal about land and water close to home. The money, the rules for spending it and the national vote are decided in Lima. Both are true at once.
WHO.yourCall: What does the comunidad decide for itself that your own neighborhood does not? What would you hand to it, and what to Lima?

decisions.q: The lowest wage a Denver employer may pay
decisions.detail: Denver sets its own minimum wage, $19.29 an hour in 2026, after Colorado let cities do so in 2019.

decisions.q: Whether Denver workers get paid family and medical leave
decisions.detail: Colorado voters approved FAMLI in 2020; it pays up to 12 weeks. A separate 2020 state law gives paid sick leave at employers of every size.
decisions.src: Denver shared mirror (FAMLI; Healthy Families and Workplaces Act)

decisions.detail: An independent 12-member commission, created when voters passed Amendment Y in 2018, took the job from the legislature.

decisions.q: Whether Denver police use license-plate cameras
decisions.detail: The city council rejected a Flock contract extension unanimously in May 2025, the mayor extended it with new limits, and in 2026 the council approved 50 Axon cameras, 7 to 6.

decisions.q: How Coloradans vote, and whether people on parole may vote
decisions.detail: Colorado mails every registered voter a ballot, registers voters automatically, and since 2019 lets people on parole vote.
decisions.src: Colorado Secretary of State; Colorado Springs Gazette

decisions.q: Whether a low-wage Denver parent can get Medicaid
decisions.detail: Colorado expanded Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act: adults qualify up to about 133% of the poverty level.
decisions.src: Denver shared mirror (Health First Colorado, HCPF)

decisions.q: Whether those Medicaid adults must report work hours from 2027
decisions.detail: The 2025 federal budget law adds work or community-engagement requirements for expansion adults from January 1, 2027, in every expansion state.
